note: Every use of a bare whitespace primitive in the five files that read a passport, with the reason it cannot make the two gates disagree about what the passport declares. Test 19 in run_tests.sh requires this list and the source to match exactly, so a NEW one fails the suite until somebody writes down why it is safe. Six families of gate divergence were found on 2026-09-07 by a critic, one at a time, and four of them were not regexes at all, which is why this is keyed on the primitive rather than on backslash-s.

entries.site: validate.py :: for word in re.split(r"[ \t]+", strip_blanks(run)):
entries.why: consent-cell tokenisation: splits an already-narrowed cell on the EXPLICIT class [ \t], which is the fixed form this whole conversion produces rather than a runtime class. re.split is on the scan list because it can carry a runtime class in its pattern; this one cannot, and its twin in _validate.mjs uses the same literal class.

entries.why: consent-cell tokenisation: splits an already-narrowed cell on the EXPLICIT class [ \t], which is the fixed form this whole conversion produces rather than a runtime class. re.split is on the scan list because it can carry a runtime class in its pattern; this one cannot, and its twin in _validate.mjs uses the same literal class.

scrub_money(): collapses a money.* capability id inside a MESSAGE so a refusal never echoes the specific one. Backslash-S, so it does read a runtime class, and the two engines disagree about six characters inside it: the twin in _validate.mjs is the same expression and the widest disagreement is where the match stops, which changes at most how much of an id is echoed in text nobody parses. Display only; it cannot change a verdict on either side.
clip_echo(): caps a cell echo for a MESSAGE. Changes what is printed, never whether a passport is accepted.
